hints: Focus on what controls gas volume here, it is not just the mass you start with but how many moles of gas each mole of solid can make.
Write the four decomposition equations and notice carbonates give 1 mole of gas while nitrates give 2.5 moles of gas per mole of solid.
For equal masses, combine that gas ratio with Mr, the smallest Mr with the largest gas ratio will give the most moles of gas.
walkthrough:
**Write the decomposition equations**

Think simply, carbonates release only carbon dioxide, nitrates release nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen. Count the gas moles.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2 \quad (1 \text{ mol gas})$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{BaO} + \text{CO}_2 \quad (1 \text{ mol gas})$$
$$2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \quad (2.5 \text{ mol gas per mol})$$
$$2\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{BaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \quad (2.5 \text{ mol gas per mol})$$

**Compare molar masses**

For equal masses, a lighter solid means more moles to start with. Calculate $M_r$ values.

$$M_r(\text{CaCO}_3) \approx 100$$
$$M_r(\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2) \approx 164$$
$$M_r(\text{BaCO}_3) \approx 197$$
$$M_r(\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2) \approx 261$$

**Combine moles of solid with moles of gas**

Moles of gas per gram equals (gas moles per mole) divided by $M_r$. This is the key comparison.

$$\text{CaCO}_3: \frac{1}{100} = 0.0100$$
$$\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2: \frac{2.5}{164} \approx 0.0152$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3: \frac{1}{197} \approx 0.0051$$
$$\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2: \frac{2.5}{261} \approx 0.0096$$

**Link to gas volume**

Under the same conditions, volume is proportional to moles of gas. The largest value above gives the greatest volume, which is calcium nitrate.

options.A: CaCO3 has a small Mr of about 100 which helps, but it only produces 1 mole of CO2 per mole. Its gas per gram of 0.0100 is less than that of calcium nitrate which benefits from 2.5 moles of gas per mole.
options.B: Ca(NO3)2 is the winner on both factors. It produces 2.5 moles of gas (2NO2 + 0.5O2) per mole and has a much smaller Mr (164) than the barium compounds. Its value of about 0.0152 mol gas per gram is the highest, so it gives the greatest volume.
options.C: BaCO3 is the poorest choice. It only gives 1 mole of gas per mole and has a large Mr of about 197, so equal mass contains few moles. This gives the smallest gas volume.
options.D: Ba(NO3)2 does give 2.5 moles of gas per mole, but its Mr of about 261 is the largest of all four. Equal mass therefore contains the fewest moles of starting solid, so its gas per gram of about 0.0096 is beaten by calcium nitrate.
